opportunities.title: Capture Landfill Gas for Energy
opportunities.summary: Capture gas from the open Mercer County Landfill to generate local energy and reduce emissions from the power grid.
opportunities.rationale: The county has 1 landfill listed as an EPA candidate for a gas energy project with 2,130,000 tons of waste in place, and the state grid carbon intensity is 1,954 pounds of CO2 per MWh.
first_steps: Contact the EPA Landfill Methane Outreach Program for technical assistance.
Assess the gas flow and energy potential at the Mercer County Landfill.
Meet with local utility providers to discuss interconnectivity.

estimates.label: Landfill gas generated
assumptions: EPA LMOP database estimate of gas generated by the landfill

estimates.label: Waste in place
assumptions: Reported in the EPA LMOP database; not checked by this tool

opportunities.title: Build Community Solar on Reclaimed Land
opportunities.summary: Construct a community solar array on brownfield land to supply cleaner power and reduce electricity costs for low-income households.
opportunities.rationale: The county receives 1,306 kWh a year per kW of panels, median household income is $53,210, and construction and maintenance workers make up 10.8% of employed residents to build the project.
first_steps: Review the Bluefield Area Transit Properties brownfield site for solar installation.
Partner with local utilities to design a low-income solar subscription model.
Engage local construction workers for site preparation and panel setup.

funding.name: EPA Brownfields Assessment, Cleanup and Revolving Loan Fund Grants (FY 2027)
funding.key_terms: Cleanup grants capped at $500,000; 20% cost share for Cleanup and RLF. No Multipurpose grants this round.

funding.name: Elective (direct) pay for clean electricity credits (48E / 45Y)
funding.key_terms: Still available to governments, schools and nonprofits. Wind and solar had to start construction by 2026-07-04 or must be in service by 2027-12-31. Storage has later deadlines. Foreign-entity sourcing rules apply.

funding.name: Energy community bonus
funding.key_terms: A 10-point adder on the clean electricity credits, not a grant. Only applies if the base credit does. Whether a site qualifies depends on its location, which this tool does not check.

funding.name: USDA Rural Energy for America Program (REAP)
funding.key_terms: Grant awards were halted in March 2026 and the funding notice rescinded in April. A rewritten rule took effect 2026-10-16. Applicants are farms and rural small businesses, not governments. Check for an open notice.

opportunities.title: Upgrade Energy Efficiency in Old and Mobile Homes
opportunities.summary: Launch a county-wide weatherization program focused on insulation and heating upgrades for older homes and mobile homes.
opportunities.rationale: Homes experience 4,795 heating degree days a year, 59.8% of homes were built before 1980, 20.2% are mobile homes, 13.5% of households lack broadband, and 23.6% of residents have a disability requiring accessible outreach.
first_steps: Mobilize the 10.8% of residents working in construction, maintenance, and natural resource jobs.
Establish offline sign-up locations and paper notices to reach households without broadband.
Prioritize mobile home parks and pre-1980 housing for initial audits.

opportunities.title: Expand Public Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
opportunities.summary: Install additional public electric vehicle charging stations across the county to close the charging gap and support commuters.
opportunities.rationale: The county has only 6 public charging stations or 1.0 per 10,000 residents, and 81.9% of residents drive alone to work while 16.6% work in production, transportation, and material moving jobs.
first_steps: Identify high-traffic commuter corridors and public parking lots for new chargers.
Apply best practices for accessible charger placement for drivers.
Coordinate with local transportation and utility workers for installation.

narrative.summary: Mercer County faces high carbon-intensive electricity, uncaptured landfill gas, low household income, and a high share of mobile homes and old housing. To meet these needs, the county can leverage its local solar resource, workers in construction and maintenance, and existing sites such as the Mercer County Landfill and brownfields to deploy community solar, landfill gas energy, and targeted housing upgrades.
caveats: The opportunities were written by Gemini from the needs, factors and sites in this report. Each was checked to use only this report's needs, sites and numbers. Feasibility and cost were not checked.
Figures marked as estimates are rough. The assumptions behind each one are listed with it.
A listed funding program is a lead to check, not a finding that the county or project is eligible. Confirm status and deadlines with the agency.
EPA's landfill database does not include every landfill.
Electricity bill and grid carbon figures are state averages, not county figures.
Some data could not be loaded (Geoapify public buildings and Urban heat and tree canopy (Google Earth Engine)), so needs or sites may be missing from this report.
